movement_source: row 'Operating expenses to total operating income (%)', column 31 Dec 24 -> column 31 Dec 25
headline: CBA's headline cost-to-income ratio (operating expenses to total operating income, cash basis, continuing operations) rose 70bpts, from 45.2% in 1H25 to 45.9% in 1H26 (ev-1, ev-18, ev-34). Jaws were NEGATIVE on a headline basis: total operating income grew 7% (+6.6% per the presentation) to $15,021m while total operating expenses grew 8% (+8.1%) to $6,890m (ev-4, ev-7, ev-19, ev-29). The deterioration is entirely a notable-items story. Excluding restructuring and notable items — $170m in 1H26 against nil in 1H25 (ev-6) — underlying expenses grew only 5% to $6,720m (ev-5, ev-12) and CBA's underlying cost-to-income ratio IMPROVED 50bpts, from 45.2% to 44.7% (ev-11), i.e. underlying jaws were positive. Statutory NPAT rose 5% and cash NPAT 6% (ev-2), but CBA prints only one cost-to-income row, unlabelled and stated to be "cash basis" (ev-3), so cash and statutory framings do not diverge for this metric. CBA publishes no ratio walk; the ppt split below is my own arithmetic on the disclosed levels.

drivers.narrative: Underlying expenses rose $348m or 5% (ev-12). CBA's 1H25->1H26 walk splits this: Inflation +$275m, Investment in technology +$222m, Investment in frontline and operations +$78m, Other -$6m, Productivity -$221m (ev-9). Staff +$169m to $4,139m on wage inflation and lenders/technology resources; IT services +$134m or 11% to $1,321m on cloud, licensing and AI; Other +$40m to $795m on marketing; Occupancy +$5m (ev-13, ev-14, ev-15, ev-16). Average FTE up 2,448 to 51,755 (ev-17).

drivers.bank_label: Restructuring and notable items ($170m in 1H26, nil in 1H25)
drivers.narrative: $170m of restructuring and notable items in 1H26 against none in 1H25 (ev-6) turned a 5% underlying expense increase into an 8% headline increase (ev-5, ev-7, ev-22), and so turned a 50bpt underlying ratio improvement (45.2% to 44.7%, ev-11) into a 70bpt headline deterioration (ev-1). CBA attributes the charge to provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ, an additional goodwill payment to customers from ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation (ev-8).

Income rose 7% to $15,021m (ev-4, ev-29), partly offsetting expense growth. NII +6%, driven by an 8% rise in average interest earning assets, partly offset by a 4bpt NIM decline to 2.04%; excluding liquid assets and institutional repos the underlying NIM was unchanged, and average lending assets grew 7% on home, business and institutional lending (ev-30, ev-31). Other operating income +8% on Markets trading, equities volumes, insurance income including a CommInsure General Insurance milestone payment, and syndication fees (ev-32). CBA frames this as "Strong volume growth with broadly stable underlying margin" (ev-26).

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items of $170m in 1H26 (nil in 1H25): provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ, an additional goodwill payment to certain customers arising from ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation (ev-6, ev-8).

disagreements.explanation: The headline row 'Operating expenses to total operating income' includes restructuring and notable items; the 'Underlying operating expenses to underlying operating income' row excludes them. Both are printed on profit announcement p31 (ev-1, ev-11). The headline row is the KPI-table measure named in CBA's vocabulary and supplies the movement; the underlying ratio is a different measure reported as context.

Both derive from $14,097m to $15,021m, a 6.56% increase (ev-4, ev-28). The results book rounds to 7% in its change column (ev-4, ev-29); the slide prints one decimal (+6.6%, ev-19). Source hierarchy puts the results-book table first, but the figures are the same.

$6,372m to $6,890m is +8.13% headline and $6,372m to $6,720m is +5.46% underlying (ev-5, ev-7). The results book rounds to 8% and 5% (ev-5, ev-7, ev-33); the presentation prints +8.1% and, on p28, +5.5% (ev-19, ev-22). Same underlying levels.

limitations: CBA publishes NO cost-to-income ratio walk for the Group. The three ppt contributions are MY arithmetic on the disclosed levels of both periods, not the bank's own decomposition: income effect = 6,372/15,021 - 6,372/14,097 = -2.78ppt; underlying expense effect = (6,720-6,372)/15,021 = +2.32ppt; notable items = 170/15,021 = +1.13ppt. They sum to +0.67ppt against a printed +0.7ppt delta, leaving a +0.03ppt rounding residual. Confidence on each is therefore capped in the 70s.

The primary walk I read (profit announcement p31, ev-9) is an OPERATING EXPENSE walk in $m, not a ratio walk. Its bars (Inflation +275, Investment in technology +222, Investment in frontline and operations +78, Other -6, Productivity -221) decompose the $348m underlying expense increase only; they explain the composition of the expense_growth driver and are NOT ppt contributions to the ratio. The walk also excludes the $170m of notable items entirely.

The presentation's 'Contribution to mvt' figures on p28 (Inflation +4.3%, Investment in technology +3.5%, Investment in frontline and operations +1.2%, Productivity (3.4%), ev-23) are percentage contributions to UNDERLYING EXPENSE GROWTH, not to the cost-to-income ratio, and are quoted in the expense driver narrative as such.

The Productivity bar of -$221m and the '(3.4%)' contribution are net offsets that the bank flags inside its other bars: CBA says staff, IT and other expense increases were each 'partly offset by productivity initiatives' (ev-13, ev-14, ev-33). The gross investment and inflation spend is therefore larger than the net +$348m increase implies.

CBA states that excluding liquid assets and institutional reverse repos the underlying NIM was UNCHANGED (ev-30), so the reported 4bpt NIM decline overstates the drag on income growth; the income contribution I compute is a net number and I cannot split it between volume and margin from the evidence read.
I did not read the 2H25-comparison expense walk on results_presentation p65; it describes the half-on-half movement and is out of scope for this task.

No evidence read states whether total operating income itself contained notable items in either period; the 44.7% underlying ratio implies underlying income is approximately equal to total income ($6,720/0.447 = $15,033m vs $15,021m printed), consistent with no material income-side notables, but the bank does not print an 'underlying operating income' level on the pages read.
